05 / MODEL VALIDATION

Show the errors.

Four independently fitted outputs. Model selection uses grouped cross-validation within the training data.

The original 53-row test set has already been inspected. Its latest results are a secondary comparison, not a fresh independent test. The stronger improvement check below repeats nested grouped validation twice.

Did the expanded search help?

Mean out-of-fold error over two 5-fold repeats. Lower MAE is better; higher macro F1 is better. Repeats reuse the same records.

Fixed 80/20 split · latest selected models

Groups keep matching fuel, gas composition and pressure regime together; no group crosses train/test. Target counts differ because outcomes are missing. Test end is classification; the other three targets are regression. No target is used as an input to another model.

Inspect a series of held-out cases

Try your own series

Paste CSV with fuel, pressure, diameter, oxygen, co2 and helium columns. Optional actual-output columns: extinction_diameter, burning_rate, burn_time, test_end. Pressure is mmHg; gas values are fractions. Rows outside per-fuel training ranges are rejected, including in the test-case demo. Batch error metrics use only accepted rows; the full fixed-test results remain in the table above.

Does the droplet approximation agree with recorded endpoints?

A consistency check uses the 29 fixed-test rows marked Extinction with all required recorded measurements. Using their recorded initial diameter, K and burn time, the d²-law endpoint differs from the recorded extinction droplet diameter by 0.049 mm MAE (RMSE 0.063 mm). No endpoint was clipped to zero in these rows.

This is an endpoint reconstruction check using measured K and time from the same experiments—not independent validation, a forecast, a time-series check, or validation of the flame envelope. These measurements may share underlying diameter data.

Inspect all 29 endpoint calculations ↓

What was tried—and what we can infer

Download the full candidate comparison. 24 candidates per regression target and 22 for classification: regularized linear/logistic models, random forests, extra trees and gradient boosting, with base inputs and a physics-inspired feature set. This is a bounded comparison, not every possible model. Hyperparameters are chosen inside each outer validation fold.

The extra features include diameter squared, oxygen partial pressure and fuel interactions. Diameter errors improved most; burning-rate gains were small. Test-end macro F1 improved in one repeat and worsened in the other: class performance is not a robust improvement.

Inputs are fuel, initial diameter, pressure, oxygen, CO₂ and helium. Nitrogen is largely their balance. Associations and model responses are predictive, not causal effects: experimental conditions co-vary. Use the input controls to inspect conditional predictions only within supported conditions.

No calibrated prediction intervals are available. Class scores are uncalibrated model probabilities, not guaranteed confidence. An average error is not an error bound for an individual experiment.

04 / SOURCES & FINDINGS

Grounded in evidence.
Honest about the gaps.

Liquid droplets, solid fuels and gas jets have different physics. These references support separate cases—not a single interchangeable fire model.

What would validate the 3D view?

Calibrated frame sequences, timestamps, camera geometry, synchronized conditions and measured flame/droplet boundaries with uncertainty. A single-camera reconstruction would also need an explicit symmetry assumption. Held-out trajectories should test diameter, flame standoff, length and timing. Tabular prediction error cannot validate 3D topology, temperature or radiance.

Should we move to FLEX-2?

The official FLEX-2 investigation is PSI-68 (DOI 10.60555/byp8-h018). Its downloaded summary has eight fuel/condition rows, ranges rather than individual tests, and none of these four target outcomes. It cannot yet provide an external error check. Matched individual test summaries and target definitions must be extracted before combining datasets.

Data provenance & definitions

NASA PSI-69 · FLEX · DOI 10.60555/mbq8-0451. Original table: 274 records. Twelve missing initial diameters and one zero-pressure row leave 261 eligible model inputs. No zero is substituted for a missing outcome. Approximate burn times retain a flag in exported data.

NASA/TP–2015-216046, Table IX (printed p20 / PDF p26), establishes burning constant units as mm²/s. Pressure inputs use mmHg. Gas fractions use 0–1. Model groups exclude test identifiers and dates from predictors.
